target.title: fix(telegram): distinguish and render streamed reasoning/commentary progress lanes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where Telegram users watching a streamed reply saw **no formatting at all** in the live progress draft: reasoning and commentary were indistinguishable (no lane markers, both plain), and the model's Markdown (`**`, backticks, `_…_`) either leaked as literal characters or was silently stripped. Three stacked defects, found by driving a live bot and inspecting the exact payloads: 1. **No lane identity.** The Telegram channel never passed the compositor's per-channel lane markers, so reasoning and commentary rendered identically (Discord passes 🧠/💬 and renders reasoning italic, commentary plain). 2. **Wrong renderer for lane text.** Progress lane bodies were hand-escaped rather than Markdown-rendered, so `**bold**`/backticks leaked raw; long reasoning lines additionally lost their closing `_` to truncation and degraded from italic to plain. 3. **`
` broke every multi-line preview at the transport.** Progress drafts join rendered lines with `
`, but Bot API `parse_mode=HTML` has no `
` tag — Telegram rejected every multi-line preview edit with "can't parse entities", and the parse-error fallback silently downgraded the whole draft to unformatted plain text. Because of this, streamed progress formatting effectively **never rendered** on non-rich Telegram accounts, whatever the payload said. ## Why This Change Was Made Three focused fixes, one per commit: 1. **Lane rendering** — pass the `🧠`/`💬` lane prefixes and `commentaryItalics: false` to the shared progress-draft compositor (mirroring the Discord channel), and render lane bodies through `renderTelegramHtmlText` (the `parse_mode=HTML`-safe converter). Lane lines collapse to one line first — multi-line commentary otherwise forms block markdown (a `\n\n---\n\n` separator turns the paragraph above it into a setext `

`, which Telegram rejects). Long lines clip *inside* the whole-line `_…_` wrapper so truncation can't chop the closing underscore. 2. **Transport** — convert `
` joins to literal newlines in the `parse_mode=HTML` transport branch, matching what the rich-message branch already does. 3. **Preview lifetime** — keep the streaming preview on screen ≥4s from first appearance before a teardown delete, scheduled detached (never awaited) so turn teardown is not stalled; on fast turns the box otherwise flashed away unread, and the immediate delete could race a just-persisted message. Non-goals: final-answer rendering and the durable (`/verbose on`) lanes are untouched — this is only the streamed progress window. ## User Impact Telegram users watching a streamed reply now see a formatted progress draft for the first time: reasoning (🧠, *italic*) clearly distinct from commentary (💬, plain), with the model's Markdown rendered — bold step names, monospace commands — instead of leaking or being stripped, and the progress box stays readable on fast turns. Biggest improvement for deepseek, which narrates progress almost entirely through its markdown-heavy reasoning lane. ## Evidence **Live capture** (dev gateway on this branch, Telegram Desktop, anthropic sonnet, `/reasoning stream`, fresh session). Same turn, in order: Reasoning lane — `🧠` + italic, with the model's `**bold**` rendered bold-italic and backtick commands in monospace, all inside the italic wrapper: ![reasoning zoom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-2b-reasoning-zoom.png) Commentary lane — `💬` + upright, bold step names, monospace commands (contrast with the italic reasoning above): ![commentary zoom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-3b-commentary-zoom.png) Full-stage frames: [prompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-1-prompt.png) · [🧠 reasoning](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-2-reasoning-italic.png) · [💬 commentary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-3-commentary.png) · [💬 step 3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-4-commentary2.png) · [final](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-5-final.png) **Why the transport fix is required:** before it, the exact same preview payload was rejected by Telegram (`
` in `parse_mode=HTML`) and the live bubble showed the stripped plain fallback — verified by driving the intermediate build, which rendered everything plain despite a correct payload. **Before payload** (current `main`, same input, captured through the real dispatch): both lanes italic, no markers, raw markdown leaking — ```html Barnacling
Running `date`, then reading AGENTS.md
**Step 1: Running `date`.** ``` **Tests** — `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream.test.ts` → **198 passed**. New coverage: markdown rendering in both lanes, clipped-long-reasoning stays italic, multi-line commentary stays `parse_mode`-safe (the setext-`

` trap), `
`→newline transport conversion, and the ≥4s dwell timing.
